name: Moscow International Biennale of Contemporary Art
funding: Private biennale foundation (Yulia Muzykantskaya); sponsor roster not published; 2022 edition hosted by the state Tretyakov Gallery.
watch: The 9th edition, due to open at the New Tretyakov on 7 Nov 2022, was cancelled on 3 Nov 2022 by the Ministry of Culture citing 'absolute mismatch' of exhibits with a federal museum and 'controversial content'. No edition since.
records_note: Its old website no longer loads and an archived copy is a hijacked gambling page, so reports, accounts, funders and board could not be checked.

name: Moscow Museum of Modern Art (MMOMA)
funding: Moscow city (GBUK under the Department of Culture of Moscow); founded 1999 by Zurab Tsereteli (died Apr 2025), run by his grandson Vasili Tsereteli. Individual and corporate patron programme exists.
records_note: Posts a 2025 results report and balance sheets for 2015 to 2025, but names no sponsors or board; only management is listed.

name: Muzeum Sztuki Nowoczesnej w Warszawie (MSN)
funding: City of Warsaw Cultural Department, Ministry of Culture and National Heritage; public municipal museum trust with transparent accounts.

name: MSU Zagreb (Museum of Contemporary Art)
funding: City of Zagreb; listed sponsors include public companies ZET and HRT.
records_note: Annual reports sit on a documentation centre site with a funding split; the museum posts monthly spending reports and board minutes, but no donor list.

name: MUDAM (Musée d'Art Moderne Grand-Duc Jean)
funding: State-funded national museum; patrons include Clearstream (Deutsche Börse, 2024) and Degroof Petercam (since 2021).
why_flagged: JTI (Japan Tobacco International) is named among exceptional supporters; ArcelorMittal (steel) also listed.
records_note: Mudam posts activity reports for 2007 to 2025, names its patrons undated, and lists its board, but shows no financial statements.

name: Murray Art Museum Albury
funding: AlburyCity Council and Create NSW. Major benefactors: Paul Ramsay Foundation, Russell Mills Foundation, Metal Manufacturers and the Colin and Lorraine Joss family. MAMA Art Foundation raises acquisition funds.
watch: MAMA Ltd was formed in July 2023 to take over from the council, which still supports it.
records_note: MAMA's Art Foundation posts reports for 2022/23 to 2024/25 and names its committee; donors are listed by tier, undated; its parent council posts audited accounts.

name: Musée de Tahiti et des Îles – Te Fare Iamanaha
funding: A public museum of French Polynesia. Its renovation, reopened in 2023, cost 844M XPF under the State–Country project contract (2020), with a friends' association.
watch: Reopened in 2023 with loans from the British Museum, Cambridge MAA and the Quai Branly, including the A'a statue from Rurutu.
records_note: No annual reports or funder list; the government's public-bodies report carries a one-page 2024 financial summary; no board is named.

name: Musée Mohammed VI d'Art Moderne et Contemporain (MMVI)
funding: State museum run since 2014 by the Fondation Nationale des Musées, built with Ministry of Culture and Fonds Hassan II money; partners include Royal Air Maroc.
watch: Morocco's first national museum of modern and contemporary art, opened October 2014 by the king; FNM president Mehdi Qotbi.
records_note: The museum has no site of its own; its parent foundation FNM publishes no annual reports, accounts or funder list and names no board.

name: Musée National Boubou Hama
funding: State museum of Niger, about 170k visitors (2013); government-funded, with a planned Museum of the River backed by the University of Chicago and private donors.
watch: Niger's national museum since 1959, with a zoo and the Arbre du Ténéré. Its uranium pavilion was historically built with Cogema.
records_note: No official site was found for this national museum, and nothing from it or its ministry on reports, accounts, donors or board.

name: Musée National de Guinée (Sandervalia)
funding: State museum being rebuilt with a €16M concessional AFD (France) loan signed 30 Mar 2026; the Guinean state funds operations.
watch: To become an autonomous public body after an 8,000 m2 extension. This is AFD's first large sovereign loan for Guinean culture.
records_note: No site of its own found; the culture ministry's site has only a March 2026 news item on the AFD loan, nothing else.

name: Musée National des Beaux-Arts d'Alger
watch: About 8,000 works, from Delacroix and Monet to Baya and Racim; reopened after its 2020 COVID closure.
records_note: The museum's old site posts no reports, accounts, funder list or board; it is a state establishment under the culture minister.

name: Musée National du Bardo
funding: State museum. A 2001 World Bank loan (~24M TND, plus 9.5M TND from the state) paid for the 2009-12 expansion; a 2017 Louvre partnership was backed by TOTAL Tunisie, Loukil, ATUGE and Dar El Marsa.
watch: Tunisia's largest museum, known for its Roman mosaics; closed July 2021 to Sept 2023.
records_note: The museum's website did not load, so its reports, accounts, funders and board could not be checked.
